questions.question: India and Pakistan had signed the ______, under which the two countries agreed to sort out differences and disputes bilaterally.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shimla Pact.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shimla Pact**

 
 
• ​The Simla Agreement, signed by **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and Pakistani President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto **on **July 2, 1972,** at **Shimla**, the capital of the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh, was a **peace treaty between India and Pakistan.**
 
• It followed the** Indo-Pakistani War of 1971**, which began after India intervened in East Pakistan as an ally of Bengali rebels who were fighting against Pakistani state forces in the **Bangladesh Liberation War.**
 
• The treaty's stated **objective** was to "bring an end to the war and confrontation that has previously stained their relations" and to "conceive the steps to be taken for further** normalization** of India–Pakistan relations, while also laying down the principles that should govern their future interactions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lucknow Pact**

 
 
• The Lucknow Pact was a **combined conference **of the** Indian National Congress **headed by** Maratha leader Bal Gangadhar Tilak **and** the All-India Muslim League** led by** Muhammad Ali Jinnah** conducted in** Lucknow **in **December 1916** that resulted in an agreement between the two organizations.
 
• The two parties agreed to provide** religious minorities** participation in** provincial legislatures** as part of the agreement.
 
• The** major achievement **of the Lucknow Pact was that the **moderates and radicals **reunited and they jointly demanded self-rule for India. All the Indians got united and protested against the Britishers for self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Agra Summit**
 
 
• The Agra Summit was a **landmark two-day conference** between **India and Pakistan** that took place between **July 14 and 16, 2001.**
 
• It was held in the hopes of settling** long-standing tensions** between** India and Pakistan.**
 
• A** suggestion **was presented at this summit to dramatically **reduce nuclear arsenals,** as well as** other issues **such as the **Kashmir dispute** and** cross-border terrorism.**
 
• The** Agra Treaty **was** never signed** because th**e negotiations broke down** and the process collapsed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• Don't get confused by the spelling of Shimla. The pact is known as as **'Simla Pact'**. It is without the letter 'h'.

questions.question: The _______ movement was led by Chaudhary Devi Lal in 1987.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nyay Yudh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chaudhary Devi Lal **led the **Nyaya Yudh** movement in **Haryana in1987.**
 
• It was a movement for seeking justice as the name says **Nyaya which means Justice.**
 
• He launched the Nyay Yudh movement by** forming a party known as Lok Dal**.
 
• He served as **chief minister of Haryana twice from 1977-79 and 1987-89**.
 
• He also served as the **6th deputy prime minister **of India from 1989 -1991 in the **governments of ‘Vishwanath Pratap Singh’ and ‘Chandra Shekhar Singh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chaudhary Devi Lal was born on 25 September 1914 in Teja Khera** village of Sirsa district in present-day Haryana
 
• **Chaudhary Devi Lal** was popularly known as **Tau**.
 
• He was a member of the Congress party but later he formed his party **Lok Dal and became the leader of the opposition.**
 
• **In his Assembly election campaign, he promised farmers to waive off their outstanding loans.**
 
• **Lok Dal alone secured 60 seats in the Assembly Election**, and along with its partners,** it secured 70 out of 90 seats in the State Assembly which made him Chief Minister of Haryana.**

questions.question: Bombay State was split along linguistic lines, forming Maharashtra and _______, in the year 1960.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Gujarat.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• On **1 November 1956**, Bombay State was reorganised under the **States Reorganisation Act **on linguistic lines, absorbing various territories including the **Saurashtra **and Kutch States, which ceased to exist. On **1 May 1960**, Bombay State was dissolved and split on linguistic lines into the two states of Gujarat, with Gujarati speaking population, and Maharashtra, with Marathi speaking population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• At the time of independence in **1947**, India consisted of **571 disjointed princely states** that were merged together to form** 27 states**. The grouping of states at the time was done on the basis of** political and historical considerations**.
 
• In **1948, SK Dhar - a judge of the Allahabad High Court **- was appointed by the government to head a commission that would look into the need for the reorganization of states on a** linguistic basis**. However, the Commission preferred the reorganization of states on the basis of** administrative convenience.**
 
• In **December 1948**, the **JVP Committee** comprising **Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabh Bhai Patel, and Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, rejected the idea of reorganization of states on a linguistic basis but said that the issue could be looked at afresh in the light of public demand. 
 
• In** 1953, **the** first linguistic state **of **Andhra** for **Telugu-speaking people** was born. The government was forced to separate the Telugu-speaking areas from the state of Madras, in the face of a prolonged agitation and the death of** Potti Sriramulu** after a** 56-day hunger strike.**
 
• **The States Reorganisation Act** which was passed in **November 1956**, divided the country into **14 states and 6 union territories.** 
 
• In** 1963**, the state of** Nagaland** was created for the sake of the** Nagas **and the total number of states stood at** 16. **
 
• Based on the** Shah Commission report** in April **1966**, the** Punjab Reorganisation Act** was passed by the Parliament. Following this, the state of **Haryana** got the Punjabi-speaking areas while the hilly areas went to the **Union Territory of Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• **Chandigarh**, which was made a** Union Territory**, would serve as the** common capital of Punjab and Haryana. **
 
• In **1969 and in 1971**, the states of **Meghalaya and Himachal Pradesh** came into being respectively.
 
• With the **Union Territories of Tripura and Manipur** being converted into **states**, the total number of Indian states rose to** 21. **
 
• Thereafter, **Sikkim in 1975 **and** Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh** in **February 1987** also acquired the status of a state.
 
• In **May 1987, Goa** became the **25th state of the Indian Union**, while **three new states** **Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Uttarakhand** were formed in **November 2000**.
 
• On **June 2, 2014,** **Telangana **officially became** India’s 29th state.**

questions.question: Which Indian Prime Minister took a bus journey to Lahore to sign a peace declaration in the year 1999?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atal Bihari Vajpayee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**

 
 
• He was a prominent Indian politician and statesman.
 
• He belongs to the** Bharatiya Janata Party** (BJP).
 
• He was the** first prime minister of India **who did not belong to the Congress party and had served a full term in office. 
 
• He was among the founding members of the** Bharatiya Jana Sangh**.
 
• In** 2015**, He received the** Bharat Ratna**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IK Gujaral**__

 __
 
• The Gujral Doctrine is one of the most important doctrines in** India’s foreign policy**.
 
• It was propounded and initiated in **1996 by I.K. Gujral**.
 
• He was then** Foreign Minister** in the Deve Gowda Government.
 
• I.K. Gujral also served as the** Prime Minister of India **from **April 1997** to **March 1998**.
 
 
 
• **PV Narsimha Rao**__
 __
 
• **Pamulaparthi Venkata Narasimha Rao** (28 June 1921 – 23 December 2004) was an Indian lawyer and politician who served as the **9th Prime Minister of India** from **1991** to **1996**.
 
• He is often referred to as the "**Father of Indian Economic Reforms**".
 
• **PV Narsimha Rao** was also referred to as **Chanakya **for his ability to steer economic and political legislation through the parliament at a time when he headed a minority government.
 
 
 
• **HD Deve Gowda**__
 
 
• On May 18, 1933, he was born in** Haradanahalli village of Holenarasipura taluk, Hassan District in Karnataka**.
 
• On** December 11, 1994**, he assumed office as the** 14th Chief Minister of Karnataka**.
 
• He resigned as the Chief Minister of Karnataka on May 30, 1996, to be sworn in as the** 11th Prime Minister of India**..

questions.question: In which year did the Bhopal Gas Tragedy take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1984**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Bhopal Gas Tragedy:

 
 
• It happened on December 3, 1984.
 
• It was happened due to leakage of Methyl Isocyanate (CH3NCO) from the pesticide plant of Union Carbide (now Dow Chemicals), an MNC, in Madhya Pradesh capital Bhopal.
 
• It is estimated that about 40 tonnes of gas and other chemicals leaked from the Union Carbide factory.
 
• Methyl isocyanate is an extremely toxic gas and if its concentration in the air touches 21ppm (parts per million), it can cause death within minutes of inhaling the gas.
 
• It is one of the worst chemical disasters globally and still continues to have its ill effects on the people of the affected areas.
 
• After the tragedy, the government of India enacted a Public Liability Insurance Act (1991) that meant to provide immediate relief to victims of accidents involving hazardous industries. 
 
 
• Under the Act, an environment relief fund was set up to compensate affected people.

questions.question: Who was the first woman chief secretary of Punjab?

• Vini Mahajan has replaced Karan Avtar Singh of the 1984 batch who was due to retire in August this year.
 
• Karan Avtar takes over as Special Chief Secretary, Governance Reforms.
 
• Mahajan is set to remain in the post until her retirement in October 2024.
 
• She has held prominent positions in Punjab and served in the Prime Minister’s Office during the tenure of Dr Manmohan Singh from 2005 to 2012.

questions.question: On 15 August 1947, the first prime minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru, raised the Indian National Flag above the _________of Red Fort in Delhi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Lahori Gate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru** was the first Prime Minister of India.
 
• He hoisted the **Indian National Flag** at the **Red Fort** on 15th August 1947, marking India's independence from British rule.
 
• The flag was raised above the **Lahori Gate** of the Red Fort in Delhi.
 
• This event has since become a national tradition, observed annually on Independence Day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Keyword
 Information
 
 
 
 

 **Red Fort**
 A historical fort in the city of Delhi in India. It was the main residence of the emperors of the Mughal dynasty for nearly 200 years, until 1857.
 
 

 **Lahori Gate**
 The main gate of the Red Fort, facing Lahore, now in Pakistan, hence named Lahori Gate.
 
 

 **Independence Day**
 Observed annually on 15 August, it is a national holiday in India commemorating the nation's independence from the United Kingdom on 15 August 1947.
 
 

 **Jawaharlal Nehru**
 Served as the first Prime Minister of India from 1947 to 1964 and is a central figure in Indian politics both before and after independence.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of 'Bhoodan Yajna' in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vinoba Bhave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vinoba Bhave** was the founder of the **Bhoodan Yajna**, a land donation movement in India.
 
• The movement was initiated in **1951** at Pochampally village in Telangana, where Bhave convinced wealthy landowners to donate land to landless peasants.
 
• The primary aim of Bhoodan was to address **land redistribution** and reduce socio-economic inequality in rural India.
 
• Vinoba Bhave was a follower of **Mahatma Gandhi** and believed in achieving social justice through non-violence and persuasion.
 
• The Bhoodan Movement was a significant part of India's post-independence **Sarvodaya movement**, which aimed for the welfare of all.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhoodan Yajna:**

 
 
• Bhoodan translates to "land donation," and the movement was aimed at redistributing land from wealthy landowners to the landless.
 
• It was a voluntary initiative that relied on moral persuasion rather than force or legislation.
 
• The movement later evolved into the **Gramdan Movement**, where entire villages collectively donated land.
 
 
 
• **Vinoba Bhave:**
 
 
• Vinoba Bhave (1895–1982) was a prominent social reformer and a staunch follower of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• He was the first recipient of the **Ramon Magsaysay Award for Community Leadership** in 1958.
 
• He believed in non-violent methods to achieve social and economic equity.
 
 
 
• **Sarvodaya Movement:**
 
 
• The Sarvodaya Movement, meaning "progress for all," was inspired by Gandhian principles.
 
• It aimed at social transformation through self-reliance, non-violence, and grassroots development.
 
• Bhoodan Yajna was one of the key components of the larger Sarvodaya Movement.
 
 
 
• **Pochampally:**
 
 
• Pochampally, where the Bhoodan Movement was initiated, is now known as **Pochampally Handloom Park** and is famous for its handwoven Ikat sarees.
 
• The village is located in the Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district of Telangana.

questions.question: When did the Indian Army liberate Goa from the Portuguese and declare it a Union Territory?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1961**__.

__
 
• **The annexation of Goa was the process in which the Republic of India annexed the erstwhile Portuguese Indian territories of Estado da India, Goa, Daman and Diu, beginning with an armed action by the Indian Armed Forces in December 1961**__.

 
 
• In India, this action is known as the "**liberation of Goa**".
 
• In Portugal, this is known as the "Invasion of Goa".
 
• Dadra and Nagar Haveli had already been declared independent by the local people.
